items.prompt: Describe how learners could select pebbles systematically along a marked beach transect. Give a procedure that another group could repeat.
items.canonical_answer: State the starting point and mark regular intervals along the transect. At each interval apply the same agreed rule for selecting a pebble, with a pre-agreed rule if no suitable pebble is present. Record the position of each selected pebble so the sample can be traced and the procedure repeated.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: first state a start and regular interval.
1 mark: give a consistent selection step, including a rule for an unavailable pebble.
1 mark: record the position for each selection as the result of the sampling procedure.
items.provenance: Original structural exemplar; not a production-bank item.

items.prompt: Explain why a tourism survey comparing two age groups might use stratified sampling by age rather than interviewing the first people available at a car park.
items.canonical_answer: Stratifying by age deliberately includes respondents from the age groups being compared. This supports the intended comparison instead of allowing the available crowd at one moment to leave a group poorly represented.
marking_guidance: 1 mark: give the reason that the selection includes the relevant age groups.
1 mark: explain the consequence for a meaningful comparison, rather than relying on the first available crowd.
items.provenance: Original structural exemplar; not a production-bank item.
